newsitem.title: USA: Fiscal emergency called for Cleveland schools.
newsitem.headline: Fiscal emergency called for Cleveland schools.

text.p: The Cleveland City School District was declared in a fiscal emergency Friday by the Ohio Auditor's Office.

State auditor Jim Petro said the fiscal emergency designation was a result of the district's financial crisis that includes a fiscal 1997 operating deficit of $89.5 million, which represents 22.7 percent of fiscal 1996 general fund operating revenue.

In addition, the auditor's office pointed out the district has been unable to pass a levy to raise funds necessary to eliminate its deficit or allow it to pay off $77.1 million in debt from a fiscal 1996 borrowing.
"We must first resolve the financial burden for Cleveland schools so the district can turn its full attention to the long-term educational needs of students," Petro said in a news release.

The Cleveland school district is the second school system in Ohio to be declared in a fiscal emergency since a new law allowing the designation took affect on Sept 19. Under the law, districts declared to be in a fiscal emergency come under the oversight of a financial planning and supervision commission.
Youngstown City School District was the first to be declared in fiscal emergency last month.

Meanwhile, Cleveland voters will decide whether to increase their school system's property tax millage by 13.5 mills on Nov. 5. The proposed millage hike would raise $67.5 million a year for the schools and would be used to help pay off the outstanding operating debt due to mature in December and next June, according to school officials.
All of Cleveland schools' outstanding debt is insured, according to Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.

Three other Ohio school districts were placed on fiscal watch this week by the state auditor due to their financial conditions. They were North Royalton City School District, Canton Local School District and Bloom-Carroll Local School District.
Only the North Royalton school district has a rating -- A1 from Moody's.
